title: Configuration decoded by a guard
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $n,s$ be natural numbers, and let $x$ be a Boolean string of length $n$. Let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$ whose work-tape heads lie in the window of radius $s$ and whose work tapes are blank outside that window. For any encoded row $t$, tuple of input and work-tape positions $p$, case $q$ specifying a state and scanned symbols, and bit index $b$, the guard formed by reading the wires selected by $p,q,b$ from the pair consisting of the encoding of $c$ and $t$ holds exactly when $c$ has state $q$'s state, its encoded input-head position is $p$'s input position, each work-tape head is at position $(p_i-s)$, and its scanned input and work-tape symbols are those specified by $q$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
